memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"The LORD hardened the heart of Pharaoh king of Egypt, so that he pursued the
Israelites, who were marching out boldly. The Egyptians-all Pharaoh's horses and
chariots, horsemen and troops-pursued the Israelites and overtook them as they
camped by the sea near Pi Hahiroth, opposite Baal Zephon." - Ex 14:8-9 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Two things are happening at the same time, and Scripture puts them side by side.

Israel is "marching out boldly." Head high, in ranks, free. And behind them, an
army is closing the distance.

They did not know. For a while, they walked in confidence with disaster
approaching from behind. That is a strange and honest picture of life. We are
not usually aware of what is coming.

But notice what this really tells us. Their boldness was not based on accurate
information; it was based on what God had done for them. And it turned out that
their confidence, though uninformed, was not misplaced. God had already
accounted for the chariots before they set out.

We often think our peace depends on knowing that nothing bad is approaching. It
does not. Peace rests on the character of the One leading, not on our visibility
of the road.

Jesus slept in a boat during a storm the disciples were sure would kill them
(Mark 4:38). He was not unaware. He simply knew who was in the boat.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Does your peace depend on knowing everything is fine?
2. What would it look like to march boldly today without full information?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, I cannot see what is behind me or ahead of me. Give me peace that rests
on who You are rather than on what I can see. Amen.
